devto.diagnosis: Claude API unavailable — manual investigation required.

The Dev.to API key stored in GitHub secret DevTO_TWTF1_API_Key has expired or been revoked, causing 401 Unauthorized errors on all Dev.to syndication attempts. The health check script correctly identifies this as an authentication failure requiring secret rotation.
instructions: Log into your Dev.to account at https://dev.to/settings/account
Navigate to Settings → Extensions → API Keys
Revoke the current API key associated with the roadsideamericatowing account (if present)
Generate a new API key and copy it
Go to your GitHub repository settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
Update the secret DevTO_TWTF1_API_Key with the new Dev.to API key value
If you have a DevTO_TWTF2_API_Key configured, verify it is also valid by testing at https://dev.to/api/articles/me/published with the header 'api-key: [key]'
Re-run the syndication system for the next article to verify the fix

devto.diagnosis: The Dev.to API key for account TWTF1 is returning HTTP 401 (unauthorized), meaning the key is invalid or revoked. The logs show the successful Dev.to posts used account TWTF2 (the 2026-11-11 run explicitly used account=TWTF2), so the TWTF1 key in the failing configuration is stale and must be rotated in the GitHub secret DevTO_TWTF1_API_Key.
devto.instructions:
1. Log in to dev.to as the TWTF1 account (roadsideamericatowing) and go to Settings > Extensions > DEV Community API Keys.
2. Generate a new API key with a descriptive name (e.g., 'TWTF syndication').
3. Revoke the old key that returned 401.
4. In the GitHub repository settings, go to Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions and update the secret DevTO_TWTF1_API_Key with the new key value.
5. Re-run the Dev.to health check (scripts/check_platform_health.py) to confirm the key is healthy.
6. Optionally confirm DevTO_TWTF2_API_Key is still valid, since the TWTF2 account is actively publishing successfully.
